findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so case variants bypass the block
findings.body: should_block? does an exact `where(email: email)` match, and the uniqueness validation on BlockedEmail is also case-sensitive. User emails are normalized with Email.downcase elsewhere in the codebase (find_by_username_or_email, change_email), but blocked entries are stored and matched as typed. An entry for 'bad@spamclub.com' will not match 'Bad@SpamClub.com', so a blocked address can register by changing its case. Normalize both the stored value and the lookup (e.g. downcase), or use a case-insensitive comparison.

findings.title: Validator has a side effect: every validation increments blocked match stats
findings.body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which writes match_count and last_match_at on each call. Validations run on every valid? / save, including repeated calls within one request, failed saves for unrelated reasons, and the validation in change_email paths. The statistics therefore count validation attempts rather than actual blocked registrations, and every validation issues a write. Validation should be read-only; the counter update belongs in the actual registration path.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments
findings.body: should_block? loads the record, does `match_count += 1` in Ruby, and calls save. Concurrent signups with the same blocked email race and lose updates. The save also runs validations, so if validation fails the counter silently is not persisted. Use an atomic SQL update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?') or update_counters, which skips validations.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved here without any spec coverage
findings.body: The domain whitelist/blacklist checks were moved from User into EmailValidator, and the old email_validator behaviour is now only exercised by this file's two blocked-email examples. Nothing tests that email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist still reject addresses, nor that a blocked email is also rejected when it is on a whitelisted domain. The case-sensitivity bug above is also untested.
